title: Copilot Studio: discover and add skills from the skills catalog
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, package controls, Graph operations and harness billing are supported. The maker sharing path omits a section heading, and Microsoft's release notes describe a broader sharing audience than the detailed instructions; neither prevents publication.

claims.claim: This roadmap change concerns discovering and adding skills in Microsoft Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Studio: Discover & Add Skills from the skill catalog

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The planned catalog lets makers discover and reuse approved organisational skills rather than recreate instructions and workflows for each agent.
claims.quote: makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills instead of recreating the same instructions and workflows for every agent.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans selective sharing of organisational skills.
claims.quote: makers can discover, reuse and selectively share approved organizational skills

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store.
claims.quote: The shared catalog powered by Microsoft 365 App Store

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap plans shared skills across Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork with centralised governance.
claims.quote: enables shared skills to extend across experiences such as Copilot Studio M365 copilot, and Cowork, helping organizations standardize proven ways of working while maintaining centralized governance.

claims.where: front matter: status; summary; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap status remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions

claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing; Open questions

claims.quote: "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and no US Government cloud.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview as release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Both roadmap target months have passed by 18 November 2026 while the supplied record remains In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "targetDate": "October CY2026", "previewDate": "September CY2026"

claims.claim: Learn does not identify a catalog by the roadmap's name or explicitly equate it with Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" admin enable disable roles approval Browse skills; "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" licensing roles. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-add-existing; read What's new excerpts. None explicitly identifies the two catalogs as the same.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The Browse skills and skill sharing instructions are preview documentation subject to change.
claims.quote: Browse and add shared skills (preview) ... Share a skill (preview) ... This article contains Microsoft Copilot Studio preview documentation and is subject to change.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A maker adds a shared skill from an agent's Build tab using the plus icon next to Skills, Browse skills (preview), the skill and Add.
claims.quote: Select the Build tab. ... Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview). ... Select the skill you want to add. ... On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.claim: Available shared skills are those shared with the maker by administrators or skill owners.
claims.quote: You can browse and add skills that other people shared with you to your agent. The skills available to you are the ones shared by admins or skill owners.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A skill is defined by a name, description and instructions for particular tasks or scenarios.
claims.quote: A skill is a capability defined by a name, a description, and instructions that tell the agent how to handle specific types of tasks or scenarios.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Adding a shared skill gives the agent a snapshot.
claims.quote: When you add a shared skill, the agent gets a snapshot of the skill

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The added snapshot maintains a reference to the original shared skill.
claims.quote: while maintaining a reference to the original shared skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: A maker receives an update notification when opening an agent that uses an older shared-skill version.
claims.quote: You receive a skill update notification when you open an agent that uses an older version of a shared skill.

claims.claim: A maker can choose whether to update an older shared skill.
claims.quote: You can choose to update to the new version by selecting the update button for the skill.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: A maker can share a skill they created for use in other organisational Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: When you share a skill you created, you and other people in your organization can use it in their Copilot Studio agents.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The sharing dialog offers Only you to keep a skill private.
claims.quote: Only you: Keeps the skill private to your account.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[3].note
claims.claim: The detailed preview instructions offer sharing with specific users or groups in the organisation.
claims.quote: Specific users or groups in your organization: Lets you add people or groups by name or email address. People and groups you add can use the skill.
claims.fix: After the sharing-options sentence add: "The What's new page also describes sharing with your whole organisation, whereas the detailed sharing instructions list Only you and specific users or groups." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/whats-new#notable-changes, which says "share your own skills with specific people or your whole organization".

claims.claim: People and groups a skill is shared with can add it to their agents.
claims.quote: The people and groups you share with can then add the skill to their agents.

claims.claim: Skill packages can contain supporting scripts, templates and reference documents.
claims.quote: The package can optionally include supporting files, such as scripts, templates, and reference documents.

claims.claim: The orchestration runtime activates skills based on the user's message and skill description rather than requiring the skill's name.
claims.quote: The orchestration runtime decides when to activate a skill based on the user's message and the skill's description.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An activated skill's instructions guide agent behaviour.
claims.quote: When the runtime activates a skill, the skill's instructions guide your agent's behavior for that specific task.

claims.claim: A skill can instruct an agent to use a specific tool.
claims.quote: For example, a skill might instruct your agent to use a specific tool in a particular way.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An edited shared skill must be shared again to make the latest version available to its previous recipients.
claims.quote: When you edit and change a skill that you already shared, share the skill again to make the latest version available to those you previously shared it with.

claims.claim: The Learn skill pages do not state the data-access boundaries of a catalog skill.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" tenant sharing controls harness data access. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview and skills-add-existing. These describe instructions, tools and sharing, not catalog-specific data permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a further approval step when a maker adds an already shared skill.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" admin enable disable roles approval Browse skills. Opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers. Browse instructions end with Add; plugin access and MCP registration approvals are distinct flows.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No catalog-specific arrival requirement or administrative switch for Browse skills is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" admin enable disable roles approval Browse skills. Opened skills-manage, skills-copilot-studio-rule and advanced-connector-policies. The latter rules replace legacy virtual connectors and do not identify Browse skills or its catalog.

claims.claim: Roles specifically administering the planned skills catalog are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" licensing roles; Copilot Studio "skills catalog" admin enable disable roles approval Browse skills. Opened skills-manage and manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers; no catalog-specific administrator role is stated.

claims.claim: The shared-skill instructions do not explicitly enumerate which harnesses support Browse skills.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" tenant sharing controls harness data access. Opened skills-manage and skills-overview. The browse section has a billing note but no explicit supported-harness list.

claims.claim: The skills overview describes Generative and Topic skills for the Customer Conversation harness.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support two types of skills: Generative skills ... and Topic skills, which are deterministic, authored flows of steps and conditions

claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to browse and add a skill, with no documented catalog enablement switch.
claims.quote: To add a shared skill to your agent: ... Select the + icon next to Skills, and then select Browse skills (preview). ... On the skill details page, select Add.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Consumption is the documented billing model for agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness ... use a usage-based billing structure. ... Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The shared-skill page warns that using, building, testing and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing starts when the maker starts building.
claims.quote: the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate licence specific to the skills catalog is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog licensing browsing adding sharing Copilot Credits rate; "Copilot Studio" "skills catalog" licensing roles. Opened skills-manage, billing-credit-overview and requirements-licensing-subscriptions; no catalog-specific licence is named.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate browsing, adding, sharing or catalog-specific credit rate is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio skills catalog licensing browsing adding sharing Copilot Credits rate. Opened skills-manage and billing-credit-overview; read Billing rates and management and billing-licensing search excerpts. No catalog-specific operation or rate is listed.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[0].note; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Package user availability is managed in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Plugins > plugin or skill > Users.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... Select the plugin that you want to manage. ... Open Users ... Managing a skill uses the same actions and steps as managing a plugin

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} sets package availability through availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} ... allowedUsersAndGroups ... Users/groups for whom the package is available. ... availableTo ... Required if updating allowedUsersAndGroups.

claims.claim: A skill package can be blocked in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Tools > Plugins > skill > Block > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... From the list, select the plugin or skill that you want to block. ... Select Block, and then select Block again to confirm.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block prevents package usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center Agents > Tools > Registry lists plugin and separately packaged skill records.
claims.quote: Use Agents > Tools > Registry to review plugin and separately packaged skill records in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages?$filter=elementTypes/any(e:e eq 'AgentSkills') lists tenant packages containing skills.
claims.quote: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages ... use the any lambda operator on the elementTypes collection ... AgentSkills | Titles that contain skills.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The maker sharing route is Agents > agent > Build > skill > more options > Share > Share.
claims.quote: Select the Build tab. ... the Skills section shows the skills ... Select the skill you want to share ... Select the three dots (...) and then select Share. ... On the details page, select Share in the upper-right corner.
claims.fix: Include the omitted Skills section heading in both representations of controls[3].ui.path: 'Agents > agent > Build > Skills > skill > … > Share > Share'. The cited skills-manage page supplies the section and sharing steps; the already-cited authoring-share-agent page says 'Open the agent from the Agents page'.

claims.claim: No API for the maker's shared-skill audience control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared skill sharing API Dataverse skill table entity reference permissions; "Copilot Studio" "skill" "sharing" "pac" API. Read skills-manage, pac copilot and Dataverse table excerpts; none maps an operation to this preview skill-sharing audience.

claims.claim: The Package Management update operation is preview.
claims.quote: Update package (preview) | PATCH /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} | Update package metadata.

claims.claim: The Package Management block operation is preview.
claims.quote: Block (preview) | POST /copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block | Block a package to prevent its usage.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Package-level blocking and user availability controls cover standalone skill packages.
claims.quote: Manage user availability | Selected plugin or standalone skill package. ... Block | Selected plugin package and its included agents, or selected standalone skill package.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: A bundled skill has no individual blocking control; its containing package is the blocking boundary.
claims.quote: For a bundled skill, apply the plugin's controls. You can't block an individual skill inside a package today.

claims.where: controls[0..2].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly establish that the package registry and its controls govern the planned Copilot Studio skills catalog.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "skills catalog" admin enable disable roles approval Browse skills. Opened skills-manage, skills-overview, administrator-guide, manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and package API overview; none explicitly maps the planned catalog to registry packages.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate component and connection controls.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.

claims.claim: Skills used in Word, Excel and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive rather than necessarily in the plugin registry.
claims.quote: Don't assume every skill is stored in the plugin registry. Skills used in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are stored in OneDrive today.

claims.claim: Organisation-level publisher access is configured at Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access controls plugin access by Microsoft, organisational and certified external publisher categories.
claims.quote: Under the installation settings, choose which publisher categories users can access: Microsoft, your organization, or certified external publishers.

claims.claim: The cited management page identifies AI Administrator for MCP request approval, not as a catalog-skill role.
claims.quote: Review and approve MCP requests ... You must have access to the Tools page ... You must be able to grant tenant-wide consent. Two roles meet both requirements: AI Administrator.

claims.claim: The cited management page identifies Global Administrator for MCP request approval, not as a catalog-skill role.
claims.quote: Review and approve MCP requests ... Two roles meet both requirements: ... Global Administrator.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-level switch specifically restricting maker skill sharing is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio "Browse skills" tenant sharing controls harness data access; Copilot Studio "skills catalog" admin enable disable roles approval Browse skills. Read skills-manage and skills-copilot-studio-rule; agent-sharing controls do not explicitly govern shared-skill audiences.
